knowledge:
- key_parameters: KdAsInput=logical indicating if Kd values should be log- and arctan-transformed ;; removeCorrelated=logical indicating whether to remove highly correlated targets ;; repeats=number of bootstrap/LASSO repetitions (larger values like 100 are recommended for robust estimation) ;; BPPARAM=BiocParallel backend configuration, used to set parallel workers and the random seed via RNGseed
- alternatives: None mentioned; users can optionally use their own custom preprocessing or imputation methods instead of processTarget or missForest as long as the resulting matrices meet the distribution and completeness requirements
- when_to_use: Appropriate when you have paired drug-protein affinity data (e.g., Kd values) and drug response profiles (e.g., AUC/IC50 viability measurements) across multiple cancer cell lines or primary tumor samples, and you want to identify specific protein dependencies
- pitfalls: DepInfeR does not support missing values in the input matrices, so missing data must be imputed (e.g., using missForest) or removed beforehand ;; Global random seed via set.seed() is ignored by runLASSORegression(), so RNGseed must be set inside the BPPARAM object ;; Highly correlated features in the affinity matrix can destabilize regression and should be filtered out using removeCorrelated = TRUE

workflows.name: protein_dependency_inference
workflows.intent: Infer sample-specific protein dependencies from drug-protein affinity and drug response matrices using regularized multivariate linear regression.
input: targetsGDSC (data frame of drug-protein affinity values, e.g., Kd)
drug_response_GDSC (data frame of drug response values, e.g., AUC or IC50 across samples)
workflows.stages:
1. Preprocess the drug-protein affinity matrix using processTarget to transform values and filter correlated targets.
2. Handle missing values in the drug response matrix (e.g., via missForest imputation) and scale/z-score the response matrix.
3. Align and subset both matrices to keep only overlapping drugs.
4. Run multi-target LASSO regression using runLASSORegression to predict protein dependencies.
workflows.code:
targetMatrix <- filter(
  targetsGDSC,
  targetClassification == "High confidence"
) %>%
  select(drugID, targetName, Kd) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = "targetName", values_from = "Kd") %>%
  remove_rownames() %>%
  column_to_rownames("drugID") %>%
  as.matrix()

ProcessTargetResults <- processTarget(targetMatrix,
  KdAsInput = TRUE,
  removeCorrelated = TRUE
)

responseMatrix <- filter(drug_response_GDSC, `Drug Id` %in% targetsGDSC$drugID) %>%
  select(`Drug Id`, `Cell line name`, AUC) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = `Cell line name`, values_from = AUC) %>%
  remove_rownames() %>%
  column_to_rownames("Drug Id") %>%
  as.matrix()

responseMatrix <- responseMatrix[, colSums(is.na(responseMatrix)) <= 24]

library(missForest)

impRes <- missForest(t(responseMatrix))
imp_missforest <- impRes$ximp

responseMatrix_imputed <- t(imp_missforest)

responseMatrix_scaled <- t(scale(t(responseMatrix_imputed)))

targetInput <- ProcessTargetResults$targetMatrix

overlappedDrugs <- intersect(
  rownames(responseMatrix_scaled),
  rownames(targetInput)
)

targetInput <- targetInput[overlappedDrugs, ]
responseInput <- responseMatrix_scaled[overlappedDrugs, ]

param <- MulticoreParam(workers = 2, RNGseed = 333)

result <- runLASSORegression(
  TargetMatrix = targetInput,
  ResponseMatrix = responseInput, repeats = 3,
  BPPARAM = param
)
